chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
All matters are subject to destiny, so much so that sometimes death results from effort.

key_terms.الْحَتْفُ: Death, specifically sudden or inevitable death
key_terms.الْمَقَادِيرِ: Destiny or divine decree (plural of qadar)

ai.seo_question: How does divine destiny relate to human effort and planning according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the supremacy of divine decree (al-maqā’ir) over human agency, noting that even our most deliberate planning (al-tadbīr) is ultimately subject to the finality of death (al-hatf). This reflects the Shia theological balance between taking means (asbāb) and recognizing that the ultimate outcome rests with God, a concept deeply rooted in the concept of *amr bayn al-amrayn*. The statement serves as a reminder that while effort is obligatory, its success or termination is determined by divine wisdom.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 16. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
All matters are subject to destiny, so much so that sometimes death results from effort.
